topic.title: Neural Architecture Search and Budget-Aware Evaluation
topic.overview: Neural architecture search automates the choice of network structure. This topic studies search spaces, weight sharing, performance predictors, training-free proxies, and reproducible benchmarks. A representative benchmark precomputes repeated training results for a large collection of convolutional architectures, allowing search methods to be compared without independently retraining every candidate.
topic.whyItMatters: Search quality depends on both the final architecture and the cost of finding it. Cheap proxies can accelerate exploration, but their rankings must reflect trained performance across the tasks and resource budgets that matter.
topic.evolution: The representatives include evolutionary image-classifier search and one-shot methods, followed by reusable architecture benchmarks and broader task coverage. Recent work tunes evaluation metrics and combines training-free filtering with budgeted refinement, including progressive search tailored to tabular data.
openQuestions: When do proxy rankings transfer beyond the benchmark used to develop them?
How should search allocate computation between exploring new candidates and accurately evaluating promising ones?
